literal: Prince of Xianyang, Prince of Zhao commandery, Prince of Guangling, Prince of Gaoyang, Prince of Beihai
idiomatic: The Princes of Xianyang, Zhao commandery, Guangling, Gaoyang, and Beihai

literal: Emperor Xianwen had seven sons.
idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen fathered seven sons.

literal: Empress Li Si bore Emperor Xiaowen.
idiomatic: Empress Li Si bore Emperor Xiaowen.

literal: Lady Feng, title Sealed Lady, bore Prince of Xianyang Xi.
idiomatic: Lady Feng, ennobled as Sealed Lady, bore Xi, Prince of Xianyang.

literal: Lady Han Gui bore Ling Prince of Zhao commandery Gan and Prince Wenmu of Gaoyang Yong.
idiomatic: Lady Han Gui bore Gan, Ling Prince of Zhao commandery, and Yong, Prince Wenmu of Gaoyang.

literal: Lady Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince Hui of Guangling Yu.
idiomatic: Lady Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore Yu, Prince Hui of Guangling.

literal: Lady Pan Gui bore Prince Wuxuan of Pengcheng Xie.
idiomatic: Lady Pan Gui bore Xie, Prince Wuxuan of Pengcheng.

literal: Lady Gao of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince Ping of Beihai Xiang.
idiomatic: Lady Gao of the Pepper Chambers bore Xiang, Prince Ping of Beihai.

literal: Xie has a separate biography.
idiomatic: Xie is treated in a separate biography.

literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi, style Yongshou.
idiomatic: Xi, Prince of Xianyang, styled Yongshou.

literal: In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed and made Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Director of the Inner Palace at the Center.
idiomatic: In Taihe year 9 he received his fief and was made palace attendant, general of agile cavalry, and grand director of the inner palace at the center.

literal: Empress Dowager Wenming ordered: "Unless born knowing, all are formed by study and instruction; for imperial sons and grandsons, if training is not established and the old is warmed to seek the new, there is surely a lack."
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming decreed: "None are born wise; all are shaped by teaching. For imperial sons and grandsons, if instruction is neglected and the old is not rehearsed to seek the new, something essential is missing."

literal: At a quiet place apart, a separate academy may be set up; select men loyal, trustworthy, broad in learning, and hearing much to serve as their masters, to shape and complete them.
idiomatic: "Let a separate academy be founded in some quiet place, and men who are loyal, trustworthy, and learned chosen as their tutors to finish their formation."

literal: Gaozu, because his younger brothers held the three capitals, admonished Xi and the others: "You are the realm's closest kin; all still young yet bearing heavy charge—the three capitals' judging of cases especially demands your care."
idiomatic: Gaozu, having put his brothers in charge of the three capitals, warned Xi and the others: "You are the realm's nearest kin, young yet heavily burdened. Judgment in the three capitals above all requires your full attention."

literal: To have one unable to wield the knife yet set to cut brocade is not chiefly the brocade's injury but truly the fault of him who handed over the knife.
idiomatic: "To set someone who cannot hold a blade to cut brocade does not chiefly harm the brocade—it indicts whoever put the knife in his hand."

literal: All of you should cultivate the person and act with caution; let there be no deviation.
idiomatic: "Cultivate yourselves, act with care, and let nothing go awry."

literal: Empress Dowager Wenming also admonished Xi and the others: "Your elder brother inherits the former enterprise and governs the myriad affairs; trembling in fear, he constantly dreads falling short."
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming also warned Xi and the others: "Your elder brother has inherited the ancestral work and holds the myriad reins; he trembles with fear lest he fail."

literal: Though what you govern is small, you too should hold it firmly in mind.
idiomatic: "Though your charge is smaller, you must hold it just as firmly in mind."

literal: Gaozu also said: "King Wen of Zhou was careful and small; thereby he gathered many blessings."
idiomatic: Gaozu added: "King Wen of Zhou was cautious in small things, and so he gathered blessings in abundance."

literal: If one had the talent of the Duke of Zhou yet were proud and stingy, the rest would not be worth viewing.
idiomatic: "Even with the Duke of Zhou's gifts, if pride and meanness took hold, nothing else in him would be worth seeing."

literal: You should be careful and fearful in caution; do not grow proud or slack yourselves.
idiomatic: "Be careful, fearful, and restrained; do not grow proud or slack."

literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Opener of the Office, and Inspector of Ji Province; Gaozu gave him a farewell feast at the southern suburb.
idiomatic: He went out as bearer of the staff, opener of the office, and Jizhou inspector; Gaozu feasted him at the southern suburb.

literal: Also, because of the affair of Prince of Jiyin Yu being wrongly executed by law, he sent an envoy to inform Xi and thereby admonished him.
idiomatic: He also sent word of Prince Yu of Jiyin, who had been put to death for legal violations, as a further warning to Xi.

literal: Later, when Xi came to court at the capital, Gaozu said to the kings and dukes: "The empress dowager, on ordinary days seeing court ceremony lacking, therefore ordered the hundred offices to compile anew; now we are about to finish and repair her testamentary wish—do you think it can be done?
idiomatic: When Xi later came to the capital, Gaozu asked the princes and dukes: "The empress dowager, finding court ritual incomplete, ordered the ministries to compile it anew. We are now finishing her wish—do you think we should proceed?"

literal: Each of you should answer fully; do not agree to the face.
idiomatic: "Each of you speak fully; do not merely agree to my face."

literal: Xi replied: "Matters of ritual and regulation follow the times in use and discard; the people may be made to follow them, but not made to understand them."
idiomatic: Xi answered: "Rites rise and fall with the times. The people can be made to follow them—not to understand them."

literal: Your subject considers it fitting to set forth the primal intent[1] and fully carry out the court forms.
idiomatic: "I hold we should state the founding intent[1] and put the court forms fully into practice."

literal: Gaozu approved this.
idiomatic: Gaozu approved.

literal: An edict said: "Zhongni in the village and neighborhood still showed deference and respect; King Wen of Zhou as heir prince bowed his body to seek the Way—can Xi and the others, though linked calyx to the imperial splendor, fail to honor and esteem their masters?
idiomatic: An edict said: "Confucius among neighbors still showed humble respect; King Wen as heir bowed low to seek the Way. Can Xi and the others, though calyx-linked to the throne, refuse to honor their tutors?"

literal: Therefore they were set up for them, to add to their commanding virtue.
idiomatic: "Tutors are therefore appointed to build their virtue."

literal: Director of the Court of Justice Li Chong may be master to Prince of Xianyang.
idiomatic: "Director of the Court of Justice Li Chong shall be Prince Xianyang's tutor."

literal: When Xi was about to return to his province, Gaozu personally feasted him, composed a poem to set forth his meaning, and additionally made Xi commander of all military affairs in Ji, Xiang, Yan, Eastern Yan, Southern Yu, and Eastern Jing provinces.
idiomatic: As Xi was returning to his province Gaozu feasted him in person, composed a poem of parting, and made him commander of armies in Ji, Xiang, Yan, Eastern Yan, Southern Yu, and Eastern Jing.

literal: At that time a prince's household attendant ought to be taken from the eight clans and gates of pure cultivation; Xi took households subordinate to Prince of Rencheng and was deeply reproached by Gaozu.
idiomatic: A prince's household attendants were to be drawn from the eight great clans and families of pure standing; Xi took retainers from Prince of Rencheng's households and earned Gaozu's sharp rebuke.

literal: An edict said: "The meaning of marriage, from former leaves has been exalted; seeking the worthy and choosing a mate, generation after generation has been cautious—therefore firm and yielding are set forth in the Changes, Magpie Nest is recorded in the Odes, to weight the way of husband and wife, beautify the virtue of the magpie, make fitting match for the gentleman, and spread fragrance to later generations.
idiomatic: An edict said: "Marriage has been honored since antiquity; to seek the worthy and choose a mate each generation has been scrupulous. The Changes teach husband and wife, the Odes praise Magpie Nest—to weight the bond of spouses, praise dutiful pairing, fit a gentleman with a match, and leave fragrance to posterity."

literal: Thus marriage joins the good of two surnames, knots the kin of other clans; above to serve the ancestral temple, below to continue the later age—one must be reverent, careful, and correct, and only then draw them near.
idiomatic: "Marriage joins two houses, binds other clans: above it serves the ancestral temple, below it continues the line—only after reverent, careful correctness may intimacy follow."

literal: When husband and wife are already kin, then father and son, ruler and minister, ritual, righteousness, loyalty, and filial piety are thereby complete.
idiomatic: "Once spouses are kin, father and son, ruler and minister, ritual, loyalty, and filial piety stand complete."

literal: The Grand Ancestor, dragon soaring to the ninety-fifth, first examined distant models, yet in quelling disorder and founding the enterprise, the sun slanted and there was no leisure.
idiomatic: "The Grand Ancestor, ascending the throne, first looked to distant models; yet founding the realm in chaos left no leisure even at sunset."

literal: As for the rites of the kings' betrothal and warnings on clan marriage, some obtained worthy and gentle wives, some missed good matches.
idiomatic: "For princely betrothals and clan marriage rules, some found worthy wives and some did not."

literal: From this time onward the wind gradually failed; all lacked graceful wives, clans were not of the hundred chariots, matches were set at base and vulgar levels, maternal uncles slight in standing—against canon and stuck in custom; deeply was this sighed over.
idiomatic: "Since then the custom has decayed: men lack worthy consorts, houses lack rank, matches grow base, maternal lines grow slight—against canon and sunk in habit. This grieves us deeply."

literal: The princes being in their flourishing years, fitting matches of command and correctness should be chosen; what was taken before may serve as concubines.
idiomatic: "The princes are young; they need proper, eminent wives. Earlier matches may remain as concubines."

literal: This year will be used to marry chambers for the six younger brothers.
idiomatic: "This year we shall marry chambers for the six younger brothers."

literal: Elder brother Prince of Xianyang Xi may marry the daughter of former Administrator of Yingchuan Li Fu of Longxi; next brother Prince of Henan Gan may marry the daughter of former Regular Attendant Mu Mingle of Daicheng; next brother Prince of Guangling Yu may marry the daughter of Staff Adviser to the General of Agile Cavalry Zheng Pingcheng of Xingyang; next brother Prince of Yingchuan Yong may marry the daughter of former Erudite of the Secretariat Lu Shenbao of Fanyang; next brother Prince of Shiping Xie may marry the daughter of Director of the Court of Justice Li Chong of Longxi; youngest brother Prince of Beihai Xiang may marry the daughter of Bureau Director Zheng Yi of Xingyang."
idiomatic: "Elder brother Xi, Prince of Xianyang, shall marry Li Fu's daughter of Longxi, former Yingchuan administrator; next, Gan, Prince of Henan, Mu Mingle's daughter of Daicheng, former regular attendant; next, Yu, Prince of Guangling, Zheng Pingcheng's daughter of Xingyang, staff adviser to the general of agile cavalry; next, Yong, Prince of Yingchuan, Lu Shenbao's daughter of Fanyang, former secretariat erudite; next, Xie, Prince of Shiping, Li Chong's daughter of Longxi, director of the court of justice; youngest, Xiang, Prince of Beihai, Zheng Yi's daughter of Xingyang, bureau director."

literal: The relevant offices memorialized that Su Sengguan and three thousand others of Ji Province, calling Xi clear and bright with a benevolent government, asked hereditary fief in Ji Province.
idiomatic: The relevant offices reported that Su Sengguan and three thousand men of Jizhou praised Xi's clarity and benevolent rule and asked that his fief be made hereditary in Jizhou.

literal: An edict said: "Though establishing fiefs is ancient, it is not necessarily fitting today;
idiomatic: An edict replied: "Enfeoffment is ancient, but not necessarily suited to today;"

literal: the field plan lies with the ruler; principle is not that inferiors request.
idiomatic: "mapping the realm belongs to the ruler—principle is not that subjects petition below."

literal: Fief and revenue grants have their own separate forms.
idiomatic: "Revenue fiefs follow their own forms."

literal: He entered the capital as Governor of Si Province and commander of all military affairs in Si, Yu, Jing, Ying, Luo, and Eastern Jing provinces; opener of the office as before; silk two thousand bolts and grain five thousand hu were bestowed.
idiomatic: He was recalled as governor of Sizhou and commander of armies in Si, Yu, Jing, Ying, Luo, and Eastern Jing, with his office unchanged, and was given two thousand bolts of silk and five thousand hu of grain.

literal: An edict, because Xi bore the weight of eldest younger brother, gave a fief revenue of three thousand households; the remaining five princes all had fief revenue of two thousand households.
idiomatic: Because Xi was the eldest younger brother, an edict granted him three thousand revenue households; the other five princes received two thousand each.

literal: Gaozu summoned and met the court ministers and addressed them: "Do you wish to make the Wei court equal in beauty to Yin and Zhou, or to let Han and Jin alone monopolize superiority over the former age?"
idiomatic: Gaozu received the court ministers and asked: "Do you wish the Wei court to rival Yin and Zhou in splendor, or to let Han and Jin alone outshine the former age?"

literal: Xi said: "Your Majesty, sagely and bright in governing the mandate, truly wishes to surpass the footprints of former kings."
idiomatic: Xi said: "Your Majesty's sage rule truly aims to surpass the former kings."

literal: Gaozu said: "If so, by what affairs will you bring it about?
idiomatic: Gaozu asked: "If so, by what means will you bring it about?"

literal: Do you wish to cultivate the person and change custom, or to dye still in former affairs?
idiomatic: "By cultivating yourselves and changing custom—or by clinging to old ways?"

literal: Xi replied: "It is fitting to change the old, to complete the beauty of daily renewal."
idiomatic: Xi answered: "We should change the old and achieve daily renewal."

literal: Gaozu said: "Do you wish to stop at one body alone, or to transmit to sons and grandsons?
idiomatic: Gaozu asked: "For one generation only—or to pass it to your descendants?"

literal: Xi replied: "Since the divination of long life for the house, I wish to transmit it to coming leaves."
idiomatic: Xi replied: "The house is divined long-lived; I wish to pass it to coming generations."

literal: [2] Gaozu said: "If so, reform is necessary; you each must follow—there may be no disobedience."
idiomatic: [2] Gaozu said: "Then reform is mandatory. Each of you must follow—there will be no disobedience."

literal: Xi replied: "Superior command, inferior compliance—like wind, the grass bends."
idiomatic: Xi answered: "When the command comes from above, those below comply—as wind bends the grass."

literal: Gaozu said: "From high antiquity until now and all the classics—how could there be performing ritual without first rectifying names?
idiomatic: Gaozu said: "From antiquity through every classic—who ever performed ritual without first rectifying names?"

literal: Now I wish to cut off all northern speech and follow the orthodox sound throughout.
idiomatic: "Now I mean to abolish northern speech and follow the orthodox sound everywhere."

literal: Those thirty and above, habit long formed, perhaps cannot be suddenly changed;
idiomatic: "Those over thirty, long habituated, may not change at once;"

literal: those thirty and below, persons now in court, in speech may not follow the old.
idiomatic: "but those under thirty now at court may not keep the old pronunciation."

literal: If anyone deliberately does so, let rank be lowered and office dismissed.
idiomatic: "Whoever deliberately does so shall be demoted and dismissed."

literal: Each should deeply take warning.
idiomatic: "Take this deeply to heart."

literal: Thus gradually practiced, custom and transformation may be made new.
idiomatic: "Practiced gradually, custom itself will renew."

literal: If the old custom is still followed, I fear that after several generations below Yi and Luo there will again be people with loose hair.
idiomatic: "If the old ways persist, within a few generations the lands below Yi and Luo may again see loose-haired barbarians."

literal: Kings, dukes, ministers, and scholars—do you all consider it so or not?
idiomatic: "Princes, dukes, and ministers—do you all agree?"

literal: Xi replied: "Truly as the sage edict; it is fitting to change and alter."
idiomatic: Xi answered: "Truly as Your Majesty commands; the change should proceed."

literal: Gaozu said: "I once discussed this with Li Chong; Chong said: 'Of the languages of the four directions, who ultimately knows which is correct?
idiomatic: Gaozu said: "I once debated this with Li Chong. Chong said, 'Among the tongues of the four quarters, who knows which is right?"

literal: What the emperor speaks is then orthodox—why must one change the old to follow the new.
idiomatic: 'What the emperor speaks is orthodox—why change the old for the new?'

literal: Chong's words merit the death penalty.
idiomatic: "Chong's words merit death."

literal: Then he said to Chong: "You truly bear against the altars of soil and grain; by right the censor should drag you down."
idiomatic: He told Chong: "You have truly failed the realm; by rights the censor should drag you below."

literal: Chong removed his cap and stated apology.
idiomatic: Chong removed his cap and apologized.

literal: Again he summoned and met the kings, dukes, ministers, and scholars, and reproached the officials who remained in the capital: "Yesterday I saw women's dress still with crossed collars and narrow sleeves.
idiomatic: He again received the princes and ministers and rebuked those who had stayed in the capital: "Yesterday I saw women still in crossed collars and narrow sleeves."

literal: I went east to the mountains; though not three years, I have already left cold and heat behind—why do you disobey the former edict?
idiomatic: "I went east to the mountains. Though not three full years, cold and heat have turned—why do you defy my earlier decree?"

literal: Xi replied: "Your Majesty's sagacity surpasses Yao and Shun; your radiance transforms the central plains—though your subject receives the bright rule in every matter there is mutual contradiction; with what shall he proclaim the imperial canon and spread the emperor's measure?
idiomatic: Xi answered: "Your Majesty surpasses Yao and Shun and transforms the central plains. Though I receive your bright rule, in every matter I contradict it—how can I proclaim the imperial canon and spread your measure?"

literal: The crime of perverse violation truly merits penal statute.
idiomatic: "Such contradiction merits punishment under the code."

literal: Gaozu said: "If my words are wrong, you must debate in court—how is it that entering you follow the edict's intent, withdrawing you do not follow?
idiomatic: Gaozu said: "If I am wrong, debate me in open court. Why agree to my face in audience and disobey in private?"

literal: In antiquity Shun spoke to Yu: Do not agree to the face, withdrawing have words behind—is this not what is meant for you?"
idiomatic: "In antiquity Shun told Yu: Do not agree to my face and speak otherwise behind my back—is that not your case?"

literal: Soon Xi was made acting Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: Soon Xi was made acting grand commandant.

literal: Later Gaozu visited Xi's residence and said to Minister of Works Mu Liang and Vice Director Li Chong: "Since there are Heaven and Earth, there are also ruler and minister; the Grand Commandant's place is at the ministerial terrace, above the house steward—the three locusts and nine thorns may not long stand empty.
idiomatic: Later Gaozu visited Xi's house and told Minister of Works Mu Liang and Vice Director Li Chong: "Heaven and Earth exist, and so do ruler and minister. The grand commandant stands above the house steward—the three locusts and nine thorns may not long lie vacant."

literal: Younger brother Xi, though not long in office, is kin-linked to the imperial pole; moreover he is acting grand commandant long, to harmonize the tripods.
idiomatic: "Younger brother Xi, though brief in office, is bound to the throne; as acting grand commandant he balances the tripods."

literal: I constantly fear the ruler has the name of empty bestowal and ministers bear the wound of 'that other' and 'this self'—now fortunately at his house, only to bend two guests; truly I am ashamed."
idiomatic: "I fear the ruler gains a name for empty appointment and ministers the sting of mutual blame. To visit his house and bend you two guests shames me deeply."

literal: Gaozu had business at the suburban altar of earth; at first light the multitude of ministers inquired after his health.
idiomatic: When Gaozu performed rites at the earth altar, at first light the ministers inquired after his health.

literal: Gaozu said: "Yesterday at the earth altar it was especially great heat; meeting dense shade from heaven's clouds, travelers were nearly without harm."
idiomatic: Gaozu said: "Yesterday at the earth altar the heat was fierce, but dense clouds shaded us and the procession suffered little harm."

literal: Xi replied: "Your Majesty's virtue moved Heaven and Earth; therefore clouds and things condensed in splendor—though again the rain master sprinkled and swept and the wind lord cleared the dust, how could it surpass this?
idiomatic: Xi replied: "Your virtue moved heaven and earth; clouds gathered in splendor. Though the rain lord swept and the wind lord cleared dust, nothing could surpass this."

literal: Gaozu said: "Between north and south of Yi and Luo, here is where heaven and earth mingle, yin and yang, wind and rain meet and cross—it is nature's response, not my slight virtue that could bring this about."
idiomatic: Gaozu said: "Between Yi and Luo north and south, yin and yang and wind and rain meet by nature's law—not by my slight virtue."

literal: Gaozu was deep in brotherly feeling; because Xi was next eldest, courtesy and treatment were especially lofty—yet he also knew his nature was greedy and constantly added sharp admonition; though at the time he obeyed and received, in the end he did not change his conduct.
idiomatic: Gaozu loved his brothers deeply; as the next eldest, Xi received exceptional honor—yet Gaozu knew his greed and admonished him sharply. Xi obeyed for the moment but never changed his ways.

literal: Xi memorialized: "The court has long leaned on culture and set aside arms; garrison soldiers in provinces and commands, some bold and brave, are unskilled in martial arts.
idiomatic: Xi memorialized: "The court has long favored civil rule over arms. Garrison troops in provinces and commands include brave men unskilled in war."

literal: Now take the leisure at year's end, on days of rotation to court, and instruct them in military law.
idiomatic: "Let the year's-end leisure and the days of rotation to court be used to drill them in military law."

literal: Bow, arrow, shield, and spear—teach all three parts together, so that men are skilled in their abilities and at the affair there is no lack.
idiomatic: "Teach bow, spear, and shield together so each man knows his skill and nothing is wanting when action comes."

literal: An edict said: "Though it is called teaching arms, the method is not yet practiced; already pressed toward the northern march, suddenly hearing teaching arms,[3] perhaps living confusion will arise.
idiomatic: An edict replied: "You speak of teaching arms, but the method is untried. With the northern march pressing, sudden drill[3] may breed confusion."

literal: For now it may be stopped.
idiomatic: "For now let it stop."

literal: Later he followed in pacifying Hanyang; for merit in taking Nanyang he was made Palace Attendant and regular Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: He later followed the pacification of Hanyang; for taking Nanyang he was made palace attendant and regular grand commandant.

literal: When Gaozu died, Xi received the testamentary charge to assist in government.
idiomatic: When Gaozu died, Xi was named to the testamentary regency.

literal: Though head among the chief ministers, he was easygoing in pushing off responsibility and had nothing of yes or no—yet among those who secretly received bribes and in darkness wielded authority and favor, Xi was especially so.
idiomatic: Though first among the regents, he was easygoing and pushed decisions away, neither affirming nor denying—yet among those who took bribes in secret and wielded hidden favor, none surpassed Xi.

literal: That year the Eight Seats memorialized to add a fief of one thousand households; Shizong followed this; he firmly declined and did not accept.
idiomatic: That year the Eight Seats asked to add one thousand revenue households; Shizong agreed, but Xi firmly declined.

literal: Xi's nature was proud and extravagant, greedy and licentious in wealth and women; concubines numbered in the tens and his intent was still not satisfied; garments and coverlets were embroidered silk, carriages and teams bright and splendid—still far off he had simple betrothals to indulge his feelings; thereby blindly he sought goods and bribes; slaves and maids numbered in the thousands; fields, salt, and iron spread near and far; ministerial clerks and household slaves succeeded one another in management.
idiomatic: Xi was proud and extravagant, greedy for wealth and women. He kept dozens of concubines and still wanted more; his robes and carriages blazed with silk and lacquer, yet he still sought fresh matches to feed his appetite. He hunted bribes blindly. Thousands of slaves worked fields, salt, and iron across the realm; his clerks and household managers followed one another without cease.

literal: Shizong greatly disliked this.
idiomatic: Shizong came to loathe him.

literal: In spring of the second year of Jingming, Xi and the others, as generals for the spring suburban sacrifice, entered purification; Shizong ordered Colonel of the Palace Guards Yu Lie to lead the attendants and summon Xi and the others into the Hall of Radiant Pole.
idiomatic: In spring of Jingming year 2, Xi and the others entered purification as generals for the spring suburban rite. Shizong ordered Colonel Yu Lie of the palace guards to lead attendants and summon them to the Hall of Radiant Pole.

literal: An edict said: "Though Kuo is few and dim, I dishonorably bear the precious succession; recently entangled in lingering illness, I truly rely on the imperial uncles; barely extending my breath of sight, I have already crossed three years.
idiomatic: An edict said: "Though I am dull and young, I bear the precious succession. Long illness has bound me; I have truly relied on my imperial uncles. Barely drawing breath, I have already passed three years.
